newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Werner sees 1997 GDP growth above 4.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Werner sees 1997 GDP growth above 4.5 pct.

text.p: Mexico's Deputy Finance Minister Martin Werner said on Tuesday that the economy could grow more in 1997 than the official forecast of 4.5 percent and he expected Treasury bill (Cetes) rates to drop in coming months.
"Right now we feel (year-end GDP) is going to be probably higher than 4.5 (percent) but we are not yet revising our forecasts," Werner said in a live interview with Reuters Financial Television.
He also said he could see Cetes rates easing over the coming months.
"I think we can say that looking to early 1998, but certainly 28-day and all across the curve rates will be lower over the next few months than they are today," he said in the same interview.
Looking ahead to next year, he saw further declines in inflation bringing Cetes levels lower.

"I think if people continue to see the rate of inflation either low or close to what the market is expecting, which is 16 percent and next year we will have an inflation rate of about 12 percent, then rates could fall slightly more moving forward," Werner said.
"But for that they want to see further evidence that inflation in September and October, when we see a pickup, is around what the market is expecting," he added.

"(They will want to see that) as we move into 1998 we have a strong economic program and that that program contemplates further reductions, as it will, on the rate of inflation." ((--Mexico City newsroom +525 728 7905))
